items.item: Each row shows the user's name and email, role, status in words (such as Active, Invited, Deactivated, Locked) and whether two-factor sign-in is enabled
items.evidence: Row markup (page.html:349-367) renders name, email, a role badge, and a status badge with text (Active/Invited/Deactivated via STATUS_STYLES). There is no 2FA column or indicator anywhere in the row template or data model (users[] objects have no 2FA field, and no 'Locked' status exists).

items.item: Last sign-in uses one date-time format with the timezone stated, relative times also expose the exact time, and an account that has never signed in shows "Never" rather than a blank or a 1970 date
items.evidence: formatLastSignIn() (page.html:242-254) only returns relative strings like '12m ago', '3h ago', '14d ago' — no absolute date-time, no timezone shown anywhere, and no title/tooltip attribute exposing the exact timestamp. Never-signed-in correctly shows 'Never' (hana.kobayashi row), but the rest of the requirement fails.

items.item: Users can be found by searching name or email and filtered by role, status and inactivity (such as no sign-in for 90+ days), with the number of matching users shown
items.evidence: searchInput filters name/email and roleFilter/statusFilter work (getFiltered(), page.html:294-304), and resultCount shows 'Showing X of Y users' (page.html:374). There is no inactivity filter (e.g. 'no sign-in 90+ days') — only #roleFilter and #statusFilter selects exist.

items.item: The invite form requires an email and a role, labels both fields, and shows an inline error for a malformed address or one that already has an account
items.evidence: inviteEmail is type=email/required and inviteRole is a labeled select ('Email address', 'Role' labels at page.html:167-171), but the submit handler only checks `if (!name || !email) return;` (page.html:428-438) with no regex/format validation, no duplicate-email check against existing users, and no inline error message element in the form.

items.item: Deactivation asks for confirmation that names the user and states the effect (active sessions ended, sign-in blocked, data kept), and a deactivated user is offered Reactivate instead
items.evidence: Confirm body says only "${user.name} will immediately lose access to the console. You can reactivate them at any time." (page.html:493-495) — names the user but never states session termination or data retention. Reactivate is correctly offered for deactivated users (deactivateLabel toggles to 'Reactivate', page.html:315,492-496).

items.item: The signed-in administrator's own row is marked (such as "You") and cannot be deactivated or lose the admin role, and the last remaining administrator cannot be deactivated, with the disabled action explaining why
items.evidence: The signed-in admin shown in the header is 'A. Teixeira / Organization Owner' (page.html:61-62), who does not appear in the users[] list at all, so no row is marked 'You'. The only disabling logic is `u.role === "Owner" ? "disabled" : ""` (page.html:320), which is static per-role, not computed from 'last remaining admin', and the disabled button has no title/aria explanation.

items.item: Password reset sends a reset link to the user's email address, which the confirmation names, and the administrator never sees, sets or types the new password
items.evidence: Confirm body: "Send a password reset link to ${user.email}? ..." and toast "Password reset link sent to ${user.email}" (page.html:481-488). No password input field exists anywhere in the page.

items.item: Row actions are buttons or a keyboard-operable menu whose accessible names include the user (such as "Actions for Mai Nguyen"), and the outcome of an action is announced in an aria-live or role="status" region
items.evidence: Action buttons are plain <button> elements labeled 'Reset password'/'Deactivate' with no per-user accessible name, and the kebab menu button has no aria-label at all (audit.json flags icon-button-name ×15, e.g. 'td... button.text-slate-400...: no accessible name'). The toast div#toast (page.html:209) has no aria-live or role="status" attribute.

items.item: A search with no matching users shows a message with a way to clear it, and loading and failed-load states with a retry exist
items.evidence: #emptyState shows 'No users match your filters.' (page.html:136) with no clear/reset control. There is no loading state (data renders synchronously from a local array) and no failed-load/retry UI anywhere in the markup or script.

tells: tracked-uppercase-labels — thead row class `text-left text-xs font-medium text-slate-500 uppercase tracking-wide` (page.html:123)

navy-sidebar-indigo-accent — sidebar `bg-slate-900` (page.html:19) paired with indigo logo chip, invite button, focus rings and checkboxes throughout (`bg-indigo-500`, `bg-indigo-600`, `focus:ring-indigo-500`)
notes: Audit.json independently flags icon-button-name (15), text-contrast (7), font-size-base (2), contact-link (15, emails not mailto: links), uppercase-text (5), and table-row-two-line (1) — consistent with the accessible-name and status/2FA gaps found above.
